original.title: Symbolic Interactionism: Perspective and Method
original.note: Book checked in Open Library (/works/OL511137W, first published 1969). ISBN is one edition's; cite the edition you read.

core_idea: People act towards things on the basis of the meanings those things have for them. Meanings arise in social interaction and are handled and changed through interpretation.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do people make sense of roles, identities or situations?
How are meanings negotiated in interaction (e.g. classrooms, clinics)?
Typical data: interviews, participant observation, grounded theory.
common_mistakes: Using it as a vague 'people make meaning' stance without its premises.
Assuming it cannot address structure (see the structural version).
